claims.claim: The literal optimized algorithm’s complexity is Θ(n+M), where M=Σ_t d(p_t) along its actual FIFO trajectory, but the ordered queue is part of the state.
claims.evidence: At a round boundary let Q=(x_1,…,x_k) contain the descent bottoms of shelf p. Moving Q FIFO produces reverse(Q) followed by the unqueued elements in their previous relative order. The front test records exactly the descents in reverse(Q) and at its boundary with the unqueued suffix. For two ultimately adjacent unqueued elements a,b, any deleted elements between them form a strictly decreasing block; exactly one deletion satisfies x<b<a precisely when a>b, so the successor test records b exactly once. Thus induction from initialization gives set(Q_t)=D(p_t), hence |Q_t|=d(p_t). Initialization is Θ(n), and every queue pop, comparison, enqueue, and linked-list move is Θ(1), giving Θ(n+Σ_t d(p_t)). Queue order is indispensable: the same shelf (2,1,4,3) is reachable with queues (3,1) and (1,3), which yield different successor shelves. The source prose's endpoint semantics—no successor means no successor test—was used; this is also required by its examples.
claims.witness: Initial shelf (1,4,2,3) reaches shelf (2,1,4,3) after one round with FIFO queue (3,1); initializing directly at shelf (2,1,4,3) gives queue (1,3). Their next shelves are respectively (1,3,2,4) and (3,1,2,4).
claims.search_method: Direct adjacency proof; exhaustive checking of 1,240,498 permutation/ordered-descent-queue states through n=8 and every reachable trajectory for all 409,113 permutations through n=9.

claims.claim: There is an exact phase decomposition that isolates the unresolved cost.
claims.evidence: During the phase of the largest unfixed value i, all larger values form a permanent fixed suffix, i is at a position s_i<i, and i is not queued. A queued element starting left of i shifts i left when removed and right when prepended, for net zero. A queued element starting right of i does not shift i on removal but shifts it right once on prepending. These relative sides cannot change before the element is processed. The immediate successor of i supplies at least one right-side move while i remains unfixed, and i cannot cross the fixed suffix. Summing the position increments until i reaches position i gives Σ_t q_t=i−s_i, while all moves partition into right- and left-side moves. The phase cost is therefore exactly (i−s_i)+Σ_tℓ_t, independently of FIFO order. Every phase boundary and telescoping identity also passed exhaustive checks through n=9.
claims.search_method: Direct positional accounting proof, supplemented by exhaustive per-round and per-phase integer checks over all permutations through n=9.

claims.claim: The parent’s Ω(n^{3/2}) lower bound and coefficient (4√2/3+o(1)) are not established for the literal optimized FIFO algorithm.
claims.evidence: For P_6=(6,1,2,3,4,5), the second FIFO boundary is shelf (2,1,6,3,4,5) with queue (3,1), whereas shelf-order rebuilding would use (1,3). The third FIFO shelf is consequently (1,3,2,6,4,5), while the shelf-ordered transition gives (3,1,2,6,4,5). Thus the staircase trajectory used for the stated summation is not a trajectory of the optimized FIFO algorithm. This verifies failure of that asserted transfer; it does not assert that an Ω(n^{3/2}) bound is mathematically impossible by some different proof.
claims.witness: P_6=(6,1,2,3,4,5), with third-boundary FIFO/shelf-order states (1,3,2,6,4,5) and (3,1,2,6,4,5).
claims.search_method: Exact symbolic trace and independent integer simulation of both FIFO and shelf-ordered transitions.

claims.claim: For n≤9, the exact maximum numbers of moves are 0,1,3,6,11,18,27,38,53.
claims.evidence: Complete lexicographic enumeration covered exactly Σ_{n=1}^9 n!=409,113 permutations. Independent vector and predecessor/successor-array implementations agreed on every move total, round total, endpoint event, and final shelf. The resulting maxima were exactly 0,1,3,6,11,18,27,38,53. The exhaustive upper bounds and explicit maximizing inputs establish exactness rather than merely observed lower bounds.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive exact-integer enumeration of all 409,113 permutations using two independent state representations.

claims.claim: A natural twice-per-unordered-pair charging bound is false.
claims.evidence: Independent linked-array and std::list machines both reproduced 49,545,006 moves and 45,082 rounds for the stated even-then-odd permutation of size 4096, exceeding 2·binom(4096,2)=16,773,120 by 32,771,886. For robustness against the printed pseudocode's implicit no-successor convention, appending the fixed maximum 4097 preserves all 49,545,006 moves, causes zero marked-tail successor tests, and still exceeds 2·binom(4097,2)=16,781,312 by 32,763,694. By the pigeonhole principle, no charging that assigns every move to an unordered pair and charges each pair at most twice can cover this execution.
claims.witness: p=(2,4,…,4096,1,3,…,4095,4097), a permutation of size 4097, makes exactly 49,545,006 moves versus twice-pair capacity 16,781,312.
claims.search_method: Constructive exact simulation with independent linked-array and std::list implementations, followed by exact integer capacity comparison.

claims.claim: No asymptotically tight worst-case bound is proved here; the authorized Ω(n log n)–O(n³) interval remains unresolved.
claims.evidence: The surviving results give an output-sensitive identity, an exact decomposition with an uncontrolled left-of-active term, finite maxima, and obstructions to one staircase argument and one constant-capacity charging scheme. They provide neither an asymptotic infinite-family lower bound stronger than Ω(n log n) nor an upper bound below O(n³), much less matching bounds. The requested asymptotically tight classification therefore remains unproved in this draft.
claims.search_method: Logical scope audit of every claimed result against the exact asymptotic target; no finite search can establish this negative coverage judgment.

target_evidence: The exact target requests an asymptotically tight worst-case step complexity between the known Ω(n log n) and O(n³) bounds. The draft explicitly leaves that interval open, and none of its claims supplies matching asymptotic bounds. It therefore does not fully resolve the target. Its extended-state invariant, exact phase accounting, correction of the shelf-ordered reduction, exhaustive finite maxima, and charging obstruction are nevertheless correct and material structural progress, so VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS applies rather than NO_VALID_PROGRESS. The headline and claimed_resolution say PARTIAL and do not claim a tight answer, so claimed_resolution is ACCURATE.
